# Noisy-circuit study — findings (informative per-layer noise)

*Generated by `noisy_circuit_study.py` (`cli.py run noise_circuit`). Addresses the critique that
the MNIST noise result is **readout-only**, so "invariance to depolarizing" is a property of the
standardizer, not evidence about a noisy CIRCUIT.*

We build the gate-Trotter CHIMERA circuit (n=8, 20 layers, random ~50%-Ising) on PennyLane's
density-matrix simulator and read the 36 features (⟨Z_i⟩, ⟨Z_iZ_j⟩) under four noise placements,
then standardize each feature set by **its own** per-feature mean/std (exactly as the readout
does) and measure the standardized feature error vs the noiseless circuit. 12 real .SPX input
windows.

| channel | placement | rate | raw \|Δfeat\| | **standardized \|Δfeat\|** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| depolarizing | readout  | 0.01 | 0.0049 | **0.0000** |
| depolarizing | readout  | 0.04 | 0.0192 | **0.0000** |
| depolarizing | per-layer| 0.01 | 0.0865 | **0.1740** |
| depolarizing | per-layer| 0.04 | 0.1682 | **0.5433** |
| amp-damping  | readout  | 0.01 | 0.0057 | 0.0619 |
| amp-damping  | readout  | 0.04 | 0.0223 | 0.2099 |
| amp-damping  | per-layer| 0.01 | 0.0877 | **0.5779** |
| amp-damping  | per-layer| 0.04 | 0.2422 | **0.8127** |

## What this shows

- **Readout-only depolarizing → standardized error = 0.0000 (exact).** A single depolarizing
  channel at readout is a uniform per-feature contraction (⟨Z_i⟩→a⟨Z_i⟩, ⟨Z_iZ_j⟩→a²⟨Z_iZ_j⟩);
  per-feature standardization divides the constant out **exactly**. This *reproduces* the MNIST
  "invariance to depolarizing" — and proves it is a property of the **standardizer**, not of the
  quantum reservoir's noise resilience. (A linear-PCA classifier with the same standardization
  would be equally "invariant.")
- **Per-Trotter-layer noise is NOT removed** and **grows monotonically with the rate**
  (depol 0.17→0.54; amp-damp 0.58→0.81). Noise interleaved with the unitary layers is not a single
  final contraction — subsequent gates mix it through the state — so standardization cannot undo it.
  This is the degradation a **real device** incurs, accumulating two-qubit error over the 380-gate
  circuit.

## Honest conclusion

The correct, complete statement: CHIMERA's features are **invariant to readout depolarizing by
construction (a standardization identity), but accumulated per-layer 2-qubit noise genuinely
degrades them** — which is exactly what NISQ hardware delivers. Shot noise is characterized
separately (`qbraid_submit.py`: ε≈1/√S); the remaining step is a real-QPU run (`QPU_RUNBOOK.md`),
where ZNE + measurement mitigation are expected to move the mitigated features back toward the
classical cross-check value. This turns the previously weak "noise invariance" deliverable into an
honest, informative noisy-circuit result.
